packet.headline_seed: News live: Australian flotilla activists released by Israel arrive in Istanbul and claim they were denied food and water
packet.description_seed: Eleven Australians were among pro-Palestine activists detained by Israel from the Global Sumud flotilla. Follow today’s news live Father of Australian on flotilla detained by Israel rejects ambassador’s treatment claims Also last night, Chris O’Connor , father of Neve O’Connor , one of the 11 Australians that was on the humanitarian flotilla to Gaza that was detained by Israel, rejected Israel’s ambassador to Australia’s claim that those detained in flotillas have not been harmed. And as she said to me – the beatings were not bad compared to what happened to men of colour that she saw, and she heard the screams. She said she was kneed in the face. She was punched in the ribs. She was dragged across the outdoor area. The psychological torture she had was being in a stress position for many hours. They were sprayed with water and were subject to hypothermic conditions overnight, because it was very cold in the containers. So no, I absolutely reject that. No one, out of the 400 plus people that were on the flotilla, no one was harmed. The interception itself was done with great sensitivity by the state of Israel, by our security forces. There are many accusations which are thrown out there … which are untrue. Continue reading...

She was dragged across the outdoor area. The psychological torture she had was being in a stress position for many hours. They were sprayed with water and were subject to hypothermic conditions overnight, because it was very cold in the containers. So no, I absolutely reject that. No one, out of the 400 plus people that were on the flotilla, no one was harmed. The interception itself was done with great sensitivity by the state of Israel, by our security forces. There are many accusations which are thrown out there … which are untrue. Continue reading...

All of the activists travelling aboard the Global Sumud Flotilla who were detained by Israeli authorities this week have been released from detention and are now in Istanbul. A statement from the flotilla’s Australian delegation said 428 people, including 11 Australians, were free after spending about 80 hours in detention. The Australians were undergoing examinations at a hospital and will meet with lawyers in the coming days before their return to Australia. Zack Schofield, one of the Australians onboard, said the group was taken to prison and “treated really poorly”: Many of us haven’t eaten for days. We were denied water for two days. … But it is nothing compared to what happens to Palestinians in the occupied territories every single day. …

Also last night, Chris O’Connor, father of Neve O’Connor, one of the 11 Australians that was on the humanitarian flotilla to Gaza that was detained by Israel, rejected Israel’s ambassador to Australia’s claim that those detained in flotillas have not ---

That is abhorrent treatment of people by a senior figure in the Israeli government. People are being degraded. They’re having their human rights abused. It is effectively a form of torture. And the simple fact is that Israel is now a rogue state. They’re kidnapping people, including Australian citizens, from international waters on the high seas. It’s basically an act of piracy … I mean, this demands the strongest possible response from our prime minister and our foreign minister. A far, far stronger response than they’ve delivered to date. Father of Australian on flotilla detained by Israel rejects ambassador’s claim no one harmed

All of the activists travelling aboard the Global Sumud Flotilla who were detained by Israeli authorities this week have been released from detention and are now in Istanbul.

A statement from the flotilla’s Australian delegation said 428 people, including 11 Australians, were free after spending about 80 hours in detention. The Australians were undergoing examinations at a hospital and will meet with lawyers in the coming days before their return to Australia.

Zack Schofield, one of the Australians onboard, said the group was taken to prison and “treated really poorly”:

Many of us haven’t eaten for days. We were denied water for two days. … But it is nothing compared to what happens to Palestinians in the occupied territories every single day. …

The message to our Australian government is that they need to cut ties with Israel. We need to cancel the alliance, stop sending them weapons parts, stop giving them political support.

Plibersek says behaviour by Ben-Gvir ‘disgraceful’ as Greens call for stronger federal response

Tanya Plibersek, the minister for social services, said the behaviour by Itamar Ben-Gvir was “shameful” and “disgraceful”.

Plibersek, speaking to RN Breakfast, had this to say:

I think it was absolutely disgraceful behaviour and I’m very pleased to say that the foreign minister has said that in the strongest terms to the Israeli government. Our Australian ambassador in Israel has made the position of the Australian government very clear that this behaviour is acceptable, completely unacceptable.

Greens senator Nick McKim went a step further, telling RN:

That is abhorrent treatment of people by a senior figure in the Israeli government. People are being degraded. They’re having their human rights abused. It is effectively a form of torture. And the simple fact is that Israel is now a rogue state. They’re kidnapping people, including Australian citizens, from international waters on the high seas. It’s basically an act of piracy …

I mean, this demands the strongest possible response from our prime minister and our foreign minister. A far, far stronger response than they’ve delivered to date.

The activists’ treatment by police officers under the direction of National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir also drew a rebuke from ‌Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and from the United States, Israel’s staunchest ally.

The activists, whose vessel was intercepted on Wednesday in international waters by Israeli naval forces as they were trying to deliver humanitarian aid to Gaza, were all deported from Israel on Thursday, the Israeli foreign ministry said.

Across Europe, governments summoned Israeli ambassadors to condemn the video. Italy demanded an apology, Spain said it would not tolerate maltreatment of its citizens, and France demanded the release of all the detainees.

Britain’s foreign ministry said ​the video “violates the most basic standards of respect and dignity for people”, while Poland’s foreign minister called for Ben-Gvir to be banned from entering the country.

The U.S. Ambassador to Israel, Mike ​Huckabee, said Ben-Gvir had “betrayed (the) dignity of his nation”.

Thameen al-Kheetan, spokesperson for the Office of the U.N. High Commissioner for ​Human Rights, said the activists’ arrest at sea appeared to be unlawful, and that any maltreatment should be investigated and those found responsible held to account.

“It is not a crime to show solidarity and bring humanitarian ​assistance to the people who are in dire need of it in Gaza,” he told Reuters.

Italian journalist Alessandro Mantovani, one of several activists separated from the others and flown home earlier, said he had been beaten up on arrival in Israeli detention in what he described as a container, calling it as a “place of terror”.

payload.title: Israelin vapauttamat australialaiset flotilla-aktivistit saapuivat Istanbuliin
payload.summary: Global Sumud -flotillalla olleet australialaisaktivistit ovat saapuneet Istanbuliin Israelin pidätyksen jälkeen. Aktivistit kertovat ruoan ja veden epäämisestä sekä huonosta kohtelusta, kun taas Israelin edustaja kiistää väitteet vahingoittamisesta.
payload.content:
Global Sumud -flotillalla olleet aktivistit, jotka Israelin viranomaiset pidättivät tällä viikolla, on vapautettu ja he ovat saapuneet Istanbuliin. Flotillan australialaisdelegaation mukaan vapautettujen joukossa oli 11 australialaista, ja kaikkiaan 428 ihmistä oli ollut pidätettynä noin 80 tuntia.

## Aktivistit kertovat huonosta kohtelusta

Australialaisdelegaation mukaan vapautetut australialaiset olivat Istanbulissa lääkärintarkastuksissa. Heidän oli määrä tavata asianajajia lähipäivinä ennen paluutaan Australiaan. Delegaation mukaan kyse oli Gazaan suuntautuneesta humanitaariseksi kuvatusta flotillasta, jonka Israel pysäytti.

Yksi mukana olleista australialaisista, Zack Schofield, sanoi ryhmän joutuneen vankilaan ja tulleen kohdelluksi erittäin huonosti. Hänen mukaansa monet eivät olleet syöneet päiviin, ja vettä oli evätty kahden päivän ajan. Schofield liitti kokemukset laajempaan palestiinalaisten kohtelua koskevaan kritiikkiin. Hänen väitteitään pidätysolosuhteista ei ole tässä aineistossa vahvistettu riippumattomasti.

## Perheenjäsen kiistää Israelin version

Neve O’Connorin isä Chris O’Connor torjui Israelin Australian-suurlähettilään väitteen, jonka mukaan flotilloilla pidätettyjä ei olisi vahingoitettu. O’Connorin mukaan hänen tyttärensä oli kertonut väkivallasta, kylmistä olosuhteista ja pitkästä pakotetusta asennosta pidätyksen aikana.

O’Connor sanoi tyttärensä kertoneen, että häntä oli muun muassa lyöty, potkaistu kasvoihin polvella ja raahattu ulkoalueen poikki. Hän kuvasi kohtelua vakavaksi ja vaati Australian pääministeriltä ja ulkoministeriltä selvästi voimakkaampaa vastausta kuin mitä he olivat hänen mukaansa siihen mennessä antaneet.

## Israel kiistää väitteet

Israelin edustajan mukaan väitteet ovat perättömiä. Hän sanoi, ettei kukaan yli 400 flotillalla olleesta ihmisestä vahingoittunut ja että Israelin turvallisuusjoukot toimivat pysäytyksessä hänen mukaansa huolellisesti. Näin tapahtumien kuvauksissa on selvä ristiriita aktivistien ja Israelin virallisen kannan välillä.

Aineiston perusteella tarkkaa pysäytyspaikkaa tai kaikkia pidätyksen yksityiskohtia ei voida varmistaa. Vahvistettavissa on, että australialaisdelegaation mukaan 11 australialaista oli vapautettujen joukossa, he saapuivat Istanbuliin ja heidän seuraavat vaiheensa olivat lääkärintarkastukset, asianajajien tapaamiset ja paluu Australiaan.
summary_bullets: Global Sumud -flotillalla pidätetyt aktivistit on vapautettu ja he ovat saapuneet Istanbuliin.
Australialaisdelegaation mukaan 428 ihmistä, joista 11 australialaisia, oli pidätettynä noin 80 tuntia.
Aktivistit ja omaiset väittävät pidätysolosuhteita huonoiksi, mutta Israelin edustaja kiistää väitteet vahingoittamisesta.
payload.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu annettuun aineistoon. Aktivistien ja omaisten väitteet kohtelusta on esitetty väitteinä, koska riippumatonta vahvistusta ei ollut paketissa; Israelin kiistävä kanta on mukana.

## Aktivistit kertovat huonosta kohtelusta

Australialaisdelegaation mukaan vapautetut australialaiset olivat Istanbulissa lääkärintarkastuksissa. Heidän oli määrä tavata asianajajia lähipäivinä ennen paluutaan Australiaan. Delegaation mukaan kyse oli Gazaan suuntautuneesta humanitaariseksi kuvatusta flotillasta, jonka Israel pysäytti.

Yksi mukana olleista australialaisista, Zack Schofield, sanoi ryhmän joutuneen vankilaan ja tulleen kohdelluksi erittäin huonosti. Hänen mukaansa monet eivät olleet syöneet päiviin, ja vettä oli evätty kahden päivän ajan. Schofield liitti kokemukset laajempaan palestiinalaisten kohtelua koskevaan kritiikkiin. Hänen väitteitään pidätysolosuhteista ei ole tässä aineistossa vahvistettu riippumattomasti.

## Perheenjäsen kiistää Israelin version

Neve O’Connorin isä Chris O’Connor torjui Israelin Australian-suurlähettilään väitteen, jonka mukaan flotilloilla pidätettyjä ei olisi vahingoitettu. O’Connorin mukaan hänen tyttärensä oli kertonut väkivallasta, kylmistä olosuhteista ja pitkästä pakotetusta asennosta pidätyksen aikana.

O’Connor sanoi tyttärensä kertoneen, että häntä oli muun muassa lyöty, potkaistu kasvoihin polvella ja raahattu ulkoalueen poikki. Hän kuvasi kohtelua vakavaksi ja vaati Australian pääministeriltä ja ulkoministeriltä selvästi voimakkaampaa vastausta kuin mitä he olivat hänen mukaansa siihen mennessä antaneet.

## Israel kiistää väitteet

Israelin edustajan mukaan väitteet ovat perättömiä. Hän sanoi, ettei kukaan yli 400 flotillalla olleesta ihmisestä vahingoittunut ja että Israelin turvallisuusjoukot toimivat pysäytyksessä hänen mukaansa huolellisesti. Näin tapahtumien kuvauksissa on selvä ristiriita aktivistien ja Israelin virallisen kannan välillä.

Aineiston perusteella tarkkaa pysäytyspaikkaa tai kaikkia pidätyksen yksityiskohtia ei voida varmistaa. Vahvistettavissa on, että australialaisdelegaation mukaan 11 australialaista oli vapautettujen joukossa, he saapuivat Istanbuliin ja heidän seuraavat vaiheensa olivat lääkärintarkastukset, asianajajien tapaamiset ja paluu Australiaan.

Eleven Australians were among pro-Palestine activists detained by Israel from the Global Sumud flotilla. And as she said to me – the beatings were not bad compared to what happened to men of colour that she saw, and she heard the screams. She said she was kneed in the face. She was punched in the ribs. She was dragged across the outdoor area. The psychological torture she had was being in a stress position for many hours. They were sprayed with water and were subject to hypothermic conditions overnight, because it was very cold in the containers. So no, I absolutely reject that. No one, out of the 400 plus people that were on the flotilla, no one was harmed. The interception itself was done with great sensitivity by the state of Israel, by our security forces. There are many accusations which are thrown out there … which are untrue. Continue reading...

All of the activists travelling aboard the Global Sumud Flotilla who were detained by Israeli authorities this week have been released from detention and are now in Istanbul. A statement from the flotilla’s Australian delegation said 428 people, including 11 Australians, were free after spending about 80 hours in detention. The Australians were undergoing examinations at a hospital and will meet with lawyers in the coming days before their return to Australia. Zack Schofield, one of the Australians onboard, said the group was taken to prison and “treated really poorly”: Many of us haven’t eaten for days. We were denied water for two days. … But it is nothing compared to what happens to Palestinians in the occupied territories every single day. …

Also last night, Chris O’Connor, father of Neve O’Connor, one of the 11 Australians that was on the humanitarian flotilla to Gaza that was detained by Israel, rejected Israel’s ambassador to Australia’s claim that those detained in flotillas have not ---

That is abhorrent treatment of people by a senior figure in the Israeli government. People are being degraded. They’re having their human rights abused. It is effectively a form of torture. And the simple fact is that Israel is now a rogue state. They’re kidnapping people, including Australian citizens, from international waters on the high seas. It’s basically an act of piracy … I mean, this demands the strongest possible response from our prime minister and our foreign minister. A far, far stronger response than they’ve delivered to date.
